One pod can't tell a local discharge from regional warming. Also, in coastal water, cold low-oxygen water arriving from depth (upwelling or internal tides) can lower dissolved oxygen naturally — though that usually comes with a temperature *drop*, which didn't happen here.

**Bottom line:** Sensor data alone cannot confirm or rule out a sewage release — these sensors can't detect bacteria or the organic material itself, and the failed turbidity sensor removes a key signal.
